catalog_quote: In Nguồn, as in Vietnamese, words are largely monosyllabic. Each syllable contains an initial, a nucleus and a tone. We examine successively these elements in comparison with Vietnamese whose phonetic system is well known. [...] [3.4 Tones, p.187:] The description of the tone system uses the etymological notation with numbers. Therefore, tones are distributed into two series, high (first register) and low (second register). [...] Those six tones are distributed into three categories: A (1, 2), B (3, 4) and C (5, 6). To the extent that syllables ending in a stop form a separate category labeled D, Nguồn and Vietnamese alike will have an 8-tone system: the two extra tones are: (ap7/áp) and (ap8/ạp). new_statements.rule_in_words: Nguồn is described as a monosyllabic lexical-tone language of the Vietnamese/Mường type (6 tones on sonorant-final syllables + 2 on checked syllables; 5 tones in Ferlus's Bốc Thọ data); the source assigns every syllable a tone and says nothing about word stress, so no stress rule is stated.
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress. Dialect differences (Cổ Liêm vs Yên Thọ) concern segments and tone realisation; tones 4 and 6 often hard to distinguish; speakers sometimes substitute Vietnamese tones.
new_statements.domain_note: Syllable = word for most of the lexicon (monosyllabic); description based on elicited citation forms from two dialects (Cổ Liêm, Yên Thọ/An Thọ, Minh Hoá district). No statement about prominence in the few polysyllables/compounds.
new_statements.identity_note: Phong 1996 describes two Nguồn dialects, Cổ Liêm (Trung Hoá commune) and Yên Thọ/An Thọ (Tân Hoá), Minh Hoá district, Quảng Bình = Glottolog nguo1239 (no sub-dialect codes). Ferlus 1998's tone data are from Bốc Thọ (= Yên Thọ). Some Vietnamese authors (Nguyễn Văn Tài) treat Nguồn as a Mường dialect; the language-level match to nguo1239 is not in doubt.

sources.note: No stress/accent statement. Sec. 3 'Phonology' (p.180): words largely monosyllabic; each syllable = initial + nucleus + tone; sec. 3.4 (pp.187-188) describes an 8-tone (6 + 2 checked) system for the Cổ Liêm and Yên Thọ dialects. Word stress never mentioned.

sources.note: Sec. 6 gives the 5-tone system of Nguồn of Bốc Thọ (Quảng Bình) with tone mergers a2-a6 / a4-a6; purely tonal description, no word-stress statement.
